Akram Hossain Amin, Advocate-on-Record— For the Petitioners. 
ABM Siddique, Advocate-on-Record— For Respondent Nos. 17-26. 
Not represented— Respondent Nos. 1-16, 27-201
parties:
Abul Kashem Howlader & ors  ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Md Kasem Ali Khan and others  ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 3. The defendant Nos. 120 and 121 supported the plaintiff's case by filing written statement. The defendant No. 7, 10-13 and 52-56 also supported the plaintiffs case by filing written statement. Defendant Nos. 26-107 contested the case filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation and barred by the principles of res judicata. Their further case is that all the statements made in the plaint are false; that summons/notice/process of the Title Suit No. 18 of 1956. Title Suit No. 49 of 1958. Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 1959, Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1959 and Title Suit No. 3 of 1961 were not collusive and fraudulent nor were they suppressed as alleged by the plaintiff. Their further case is that Khalilur Rahman the plaintiff's father signed all the necessary papers of the Title Suit No. 18 of 1956 and the Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 and after his death the plaintiff and his brother Ismail, the defendant No. 4 and others file application under their own signature for substitution. None of this signature were forged and fabricated; plaintiff's brother Ismail got the Vokalatnama presented on 21-5-1958 through Saijuddin Howlader, the defendant No. 20 against whom allegations of fraud, collusion and fabrication have been made in the plaint, was then serving in a High School of Bhola and he did not know about the institution of the suit or cases. Ainuddin Sheikh who was defendant No. 4 in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 (defendant No. 19 in the present suit) filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1959 which was dismissed on contest on 13-7-1959. Thereafter, Dhola Bibi defendant No.1 in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 and (now defendant No. 116 in this suit), filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 1959 and it was also dismissed on 23-6-1960. In the said Miscellaneous Case the plaintiff and his brother along with their co-sharers and the defendant Nos. 20-38 together filed a solenama and Ismail; the plaintiff's brother, had also deposed for Dhola Bibi in the said Miscellaneous Case; Mokter Ali who was defendant No. 11 in the Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 (now defendant No. 61 in this suit) filed Title Suit No. 3, of 1961; in that suit the defendant Nos. 20-38 -including the present plaintiff filed a joint written statement for setting aside the decree and plaintiff's brother Ismail deposed in that suit. The defendant No. 20 also filed a separate written statement. But in none of the suits and cases the plaintiff's signatures were forged as alleged in the plaint. The defendant's further case is that plaintiff's allegation that he had all along been in West Pakistan from 1952-1964 is false. Their case is that Baser Sarder purchased the khas and tenanted land of the Khewat Nos. 41/1 and 41/2 and possessed it and thereafter he granted a Mirash Ijara to the extent of 12 annas share to Abdul Kader and others, the predecessors of defendant Nos. 20-44 by vinue of a patta dated 17-10-1911 and thereafter Abdul Sheikh and Munir Khan acquired 12 annas share of khas and tenanted lands of the Kayem Karsha and Khalilur Rahman and others acquired the remaining 4 annas share. It is further alleged that on auction purchasing the Mirash Ijara recorded in Khatian No. 270 for arrears of rent, these defendants got the same merged in the Kayem Karsha and have been possessing as such a land of 6.91, 3.51 in total 10.42 acres appertaining to the khas land of Mirash Ijara as well as Kayem Karsha. These 10.42 acres subsequently increased to 10.60 acres. In short, these defendants have denied the allegation of the plaint and that Baser Sarder, Abdul Shiekh and Munir Khan were benamders. They also denied the deed of partition and they also raised an objection regarding the maintainability of this suit without impleading the heirs of the principal defendants in the suit. They have further denied that Sadan Howlader or his heirs did not possess any land on the basis of kabala from Abdul Shaikh and Munir Khan.
